headline: IRGC MISSILES STRIKE HORMUZ LNG CARRIER: GOLD DROPS $49 TO $4,116 AS OIL-INFLATION LOOP INVERTS SAFE HAVEN TRADE
snippet: Iran's IRGC struck the Al Rekayyat LNG carrier in the Strait of Hormuz on July 7, driving gold counter-intuitively lower by $49 to an intraday low of $4,116 as higher oil prices stoked inflation fears and reinforced expectations for Fed rate hikes — a mechanism Kitco's PM desk identifies as the defining paradox of 2026 precious metals trading: geopolitical escalation at the Strait pushes energy costs up, not down, keeping real yields elevated and sustaining the monetary headwind to gold. Silver also weakened, falling briefly below $60 before recovering, as the combined Hormuz-Fed dual overhang compressed the metals' post-payrolls recovery.

headline: FED CHAIR WARSH WITHHELD HIS DOT PLOT — FIRST CHAIR SINCE 2012 TO GO DARK ON RATES AHEAD OF TODAY'S FOMC MINUTES
snippet: GoldSilver.com analysis published ahead of the July 8 FOMC minutes release identifies a structural anomaly: Chair Kevin Warsh did not submit a rate projection at the June 16-17 meeting, making him the first Fed Chair since the dot plot launched in January 2012 to withhold a projection — a deliberate signal that the committee's new chair views the rate-path decision as genuinely binary. For gold investors, a Fed chair without a declared dot-plot position is either buying political room to pause or preparing markets for a surprise move, and the July 8 minutes are the first opportunity to read which way Warsh is leaning.

headline: ONTARIO'S LARGEST COPPER RESOURCE CLEARS DRILL PERMIT — XXIX METAL THIERRY 20,000M, FIRST SYSTEMATIC PROGRAM IN 40+ YEARS (TSXV:XXIX)
source_name: Investing News Network / XXIX Metal Corp.
snippet: XXIX Metal Corp. (TSXV: XXIX) received its exploration permit from the Province of Ontario on July 6 for a 20,000-metre two-phase diamond drill program at the 100%-owned Thierry Copper Project near Pickle Lake — Ontario's largest primary copper resource at 7,907 hectares, last systematically drilled in the 1970s. Thierry's K1 deposit is interpreted as a near-surface bulk-tonnage copper-PGE system suited to open-pit development, and XXIX's $19M+ cash position means Phase 1 begins immediately — transforming Thierry from a dormant legacy resource into the most significant new copper drill target in Ontario in decades.

headline: CENTERRA AND TECK EACH HOLD 9.9% AS METAL ENERGY FIRES INAUGURAL 6,000M ON UNTESTED TOODOGGONE COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY (TSXV:MERG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Metal Energy Corp.
snippet: Metal Energy Corp. (TSXV: MERG) activated its first drill at the NIV Copper-Gold Project in BC's Toodoggone District on July 6 — a 6,000-metre inaugural program testing a 5km copper-gold-molybdenum soil anomaly 32km south of Centerra Gold's Kemess mine complex. The strategic validation is the key detail: Centerra Gold and Teck Resources have each taken 9.9% positions in Metal Energy ahead of the first drill turn, a near-double endorsement from senior producers that gives institutional weight to the porphyry thesis before a single assay is released.

headline: SPARTAN METALS CONFIRMS THIRD PAST-PRODUCING TUNGSTEN MINE AT 6.76% WO3 — EAGLE IS HIGHEST-GRADE US TUNGSTEN DISTRICT (TSXV:W)
snippet: Spartan Metals Corp. (TSXV: W) announced July 7 that rock chip sampling at the historic Rees Tungsten Mine within its Eagle Project in Nevada returned 6.76% and 3.75% WO3, confirming US Bureau of Mines historic grades of up to 8.48% WO3 — making Rees the third past-producing tungsten mine at Eagle where high-grade results have been validated. With China's tungsten export restrictions in effect since December 2024, Eagle's three confirmed past producers at greater than 1% WO3 represent a rare domestic supply story for one of the few critical minerals with no meaningful non-Chinese production at scale.

headline: GOLD DOWN 7% YTD BUT UP 33% OVER 12 MONTHS — ASIA GAINED 12.9% IN H1 WHILE NORTH AMERICA LOST 15% IN BIFURCATED BULL
snippet: Money Metals Exchange analyst Mike Maharrey, writing for FXStreet on July 7, frames gold's $4,100 correction in its proper context: despite a 7% year-to-date slide from January's $5,500+ all-time high, gold still leads nearly all global asset classes over the trailing 12 months with a 33% gain — only emerging market stocks have done better. The piece's most actionable finding is the trading-hours divergence: during Asian sessions gold rose 12.9% in H1 2026, while North American-hours trading dragged it 15% lower — a structural signal that Eastern buyers view this correction as accumulation while Western institutionals remain positioned for Fed tightening.

headline: NdPr ALLOY SURGES 21.4% IN JULY TO $133/KG NEW 2026 HIGH — CHINA MIIT H2 QUOTA NOW 3 WEEKS OVERDUE, SCARCITY PREMIUM DEEPENS
snippet: Crux Investor analysis confirms NdPr alloy at $133.02/kg — a new 2026 high, up 21.4% from the June benchmark — with neodymium metal at $145.88/kg (+19.6%) and praseodymium metal at $149.19/kg (+19.5%) as China's MIIT H2 mining quota announcement remains absent for a third consecutive week past its typical release window. For Western rare earth investors, the overdue quota is the single most important near-term catalyst: tightening confirms the scarcity trade; an expansion reverses it — and with no announcement as of early July 2026, the market is currently pricing in continued restriction.

headline: GOLD SEEKER #78: MINING STOCKS TAKE IT ON THE CHIN POST-EARNINGS — $4,100 BECOMES THE MACRO FLOOR TEST
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold Seeker Issue #78 notes that after a heavy spring earnings season for senior gold producers, news flow at the junior level has slowed and mining equity indexes have underperformed the physical metal — with gold stocks broadly down even as gold holds near $4,100, creating a widening fundamental disconnect between gold price and miner valuations. The current setup — slowing news flow, earnings season concluded, junior miners lagging gold — historically precedes either a sharp re-rating as sector attention returns, or further dip if macro headwinds (Fed rate expectations, Hormuz-driven oil inflation) persist through August.

headline: GOLDEN TRIANGLE STEP-OUT: STAR COPPER ADDS SECOND RIG ON 15,000M PROGRAM TO CHASE NE EXTENSION OF HYPOGENE SYSTEM (CSE:STCU)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Star Copper Corp.
snippet: Star Copper Corp. (CSE: STCU) mobilized a second drill rig on July 7 to begin step-out drilling at the Star Project in BC's Golden Triangle, extending the northeast boundary of the Star Main hypogene copper-gold system within a 15,000-metre campaign — building on an earlier intercept of 183 metres at 0.28% CuEq including 108 metres at 0.36% CuEq from surface in hole S-054A. A two-rig configuration in the Golden Triangle signals that initial results justified committing additional capital before full assay returns, the strongest early-program signal a junior explorer can send.

headline: URANIUM UTILITIES PIVOT TO LONG-TERM CONTRACTS AT $75-85/LB AS SPOT FLATLINES AT $85.85 — PHASE CHANGE FROM SPOT TO TERM MARKET
snippet: INN's Uranium Price Trends Q2 2026 Review notes a structural shift in buying behavior: utilities that drove spot prices to $101.41/lb in January 2026 have rotated away from spot and are now securing supply through multi-year long-term contracts at $75-85/lb — a migration that suppresses spot volatility while locking in baseload uranium supply ahead of reactor restarts in Japan, new builds in China and India, and SMR offtake agreements signed by Microsoft and Meta for AI data center power. The term-market migration historically precedes a second-leg spot rally, as spot liquidity thins and committed supply is pre-purchased before reaching the open market.
